question: Why does a distributed rate limiter need the read-decide-write to be a single atomic step? What goes wrong with GET, then decide in the app, then SET?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki read aur write ke beech ka gap hi race condition hai. Agar app pehle `GET` karke tokens padhe, app mein decide kare 'haan, 1 token bacha hai', aur phir `SET` kare, toh do instances ek hi millisecond mein dono '1 token bacha hai' padh sakte hain. Dono allow karenge, dono `SET tokens=0` likhenge -- last token do baar kharch ho gaya. Isko lost update ya check-then-act race kehte hain.

Suppose 3 app servers hain aur ek user ke liye bucket mein sirf 1 token bacha hai. Teeno servers ke paas ek ek request aati hai. Teeno GET karte hain, teeno ko 1 dikhta hai, teeno allow karte hain. Limit 1 thi, 3 requests chali gayi. Load jitna zyada, gap utna zyada exploit hota hai -- aur attacker exactly yahi karta hai: parallel burst.

Is project mein poora read-decide-write ek Lua script hai (`token_bucket.lua`, `sliding_counter.lua`). Redis ek time pe ek hi script chalata hai; script ke beech koi doosra command nahi ghus sakta. Toh `HMGET` (read), refill aur `tokens >= cost` (decide), aur `HSET` (write) -- sab ek indivisible step hai. Doosri request script ke khatam hone ke baad hi state padhegi, aur usse naya tokens value dikhega.

README yahi kehta hai: 'The whole read-decide-write runs as ONE Lua script, so it is atomic', aur test isko prove karta hai: 3 alag clients, 300 concurrent requests, capacity 50 -> exactly 50 allowed.
why_needed: Bina atomicity ke distributed limiter sirf low traffic par sahi dikhta hai; jab sach mein zaroorat hoti hai (burst, attack) tabhi limit tootti hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek hi movie ticket ki last seat do counters se bik rahi hai: dono counter clerk screen dekhte hain 'seat free', dono ticket kaat dete hain. Ek central booking system jo 'check aur book' ek saath karta hai, yeh nahi hone deta.
how_it_works: Redis commands single-threaded execute hote hain, aur `EVALSHA` se chala Lua script ek unit ki tarah chalta hai -- script ke andar ke saare `redis.call` ke beech doosre clients ke commands interleave nahi hote. Isliye state read karna, decision lena aur state likhna ek atomic transaction ban jaata hai, bina locks ke.
in_this_project: `src/redis-store.ts` ka `RedisStore.consume` sirf `evalsha(sha, [key], args)` bhejta hai; app mein koi GET/SET nahi hai. Decision Lua ke andar hota hai: `token_bucket.lua` mein `HMGET` -> lazy refill -> `if tokens >= cost` -> `HSET` + `PEXPIRE`. `test/redis.test.ts` ka test 'atomic across instances: 3 clients, 300 concurrent requests, capacity 50 -> exactly 50 allowed' isko real Redis par check karta hai.
code_example:
-- real, src/lua/token_bucket.lua (trimmed): read, decide, write in ONE script
local state = redis.call('HMGET', KEYS[1], 'tokens', 'ts')
-- ... lazy refill ...
if tokens >= cost then
  tokens = tokens - cost
  allowed = 1
else
  retry = math.ceil((cost - tokens) * 1000 / rate)
end
redis.call('HSET', KEYS[1], 'tokens', tostring(tokens), 'ts', tostring(now))

Ek round trip mein poora decision
Kitne bhi app instances ho, ek hi sach (Redis) hai
disadvantages: Script chalte waqt Redis koi aur command nahi chalata -- script chhota aur O(1) rakhna zaroori hai
Logic do jagah hai (TypeScript aur Lua), isliye parity test chahiye

Single instance par test karke race 'nahi dikhi' maan lena
Decision app mein lena aur sirf counter Redis mein rakhna

question: How do the atomicity tests in test/redis.test.ts prove the Redis store is race-free across instances, and why are the parameters (refill 0.001 per second, a 60 second window) chosen that way?
answer_hinglish:
Do tests hain, dono real Redis ke saamne. Pehla: token bucket `capacity: 50, refillPerSec: 0.001`, teen `RateLimiter` jinke paas teen ALAG ioredis clients hain (teen alag connections, jaise teen app instances), aur `Promise.all` se 300 requests ek saath -- `limiters[i % 3]` se round-robin. Assertion: allowed exactly 50. Doosra: sliding window `limit: 40, windowMs: 60_000`, do clients, 200 concurrent requests, allowed exactly 40.

'Exactly' important hai. 'At most 50' sirf over-allowing pakadta; agar koi bug kuch requests ko galat deny kar de (jaise denied request ko bhi count karna), woh bhi fail hona chahiye. Exactly 50 dono direction check karta hai.

Parameters kyun? `refillPerSec: 0.001` ka matlab ek token 1000 second mein -- test ke chalne ke dauraan refill practically zero hai. Agar refill tez hota, toh test ke beech naye tokens aa jaate aur allowed 51 ya 52 ho sakta, aur test flaky ho jaata ya bug chhupa leta. Same reason se sliding window 60 second ka hai: 200 requests itni jaldi chalti hain ki window ka boundary cross hone ka chance kam hai.

Alag clients kyun? Ek hi ioredis connection par commands pipeline mein order se jaate hain; teen connections se Redis ko sach mein alag sources se interleaved commands milte hain -- production jaisa. Agar decision app mein hota (GET phir SET), toh 300 parallel requests mein kai ek hi purana value padhte aur allowed 50 se upar jaata. Mutation U2 (Lua: denied request still counted) bhi in real-Redis tests se pakda gaya.
why_needed: Concurrency bugs normal unit tests mein nahi dikhte. Inhe pakadne ke liye sach mein parallel load, alag connections, aur ek exact count chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Ek darwaze par 50 passes hain aur teen gate-keepers hain. Test yeh hai: 300 log teeno gates par ek saath dhakka dein, aur andar exactly 50 hi pahunche -- na 49, na 51.
how_it_works: `Promise.all` saare 300 `consume` ek saath shuru karta hai; har ek `EVALSHA` bhejta hai. Redis inhe ek ek karke serialize karta hai; har script naya state dekhta hai. 50 ke baad har script `tokens >= cost` false paata hai aur `allowed = 0` deta hai.
in_this_project: `test/redis.test.ts`: 'atomic across instances: 3 clients, 300 concurrent requests, capacity 50 -> exactly 50 allowed' aur 'sliding window is atomic too: 200 concurrent, limit 40 -> exactly 40 allowed'. Clients `client()` helper se bante hain (har call naya `new Redis(URL_)`). Redis na mile toh `describe.skipIf(!available)` se tests SKIP hote hain aur notice print hota hai -- silently pass nahi.
advantages: Exact count dono direction ke bugs pakadta hai
Real Redis, real connections -- mock nahi
Fast aur deterministic (refill negligible)
disadvantages: Ek hi machine par chalta hai; network latency ya Redis failover simulate nahi karta
Redis na ho toh tests skip hote hain -- CI mein Redis zaroori hai
common_mistakes: Concurrency test ek hi client se chalana
Tez refill rate rakhna jisse count flaky ho jaye
Sirf `<= limit` assert karna

Mock Redis se yeh test kyun bekaar hota?
Sliding window test window boundary cross kare toh kya hoga?

question: Why does RedisStore use Redis's own clock (TIME) by default instead of the app server's Date.now(), and how does the store tell the script which clock to use?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki multiple app servers ki clocks kabhi exactly same nahi hoti -- NTP ke baad bhi milliseconds se seconds tak drift ho sakta hai. Rate limiter ka poora math 'now' par chalta hai: token bucket mein `elapsed = now - ts` se refill, sliding window mein `now - (now % window)` se window start. Agar har instance apna 'now' bheje, toh ek hi key ke liye alag alag instances alag time bolenge.

Code se ek concrete problem nikalta hai: token bucket har request par `ts = now` store karta hai. Suppose instance A ki clock 5 second aage hai. A request karta hai, `ts` = A ka time. Phir B (peeche wala) request karta hai: `elapsed = max(now - ts, 0) = 0`, aur ab `ts` B ka time ban jaata hai -- 5 second peeche. Agla A request `elapsed` ~5 second dekhega aur 5 seconds ka refill de dega jo sach mein hua hi nahi. A aur B alternate karein toh har baar free tokens. Yeh meri code-reading analysis hai, test nahi; isliye default Redis TIME hai.

Mechanism: `RedisStoreOptions.now` undefined hai toh store time argument EMPTY string bhejta hai: `const now = this.options.now === undefined ? "" : String(this.options.now())`. Lua mein `if ARGV[3] == '' then local t = redis.call('TIME') ...` -- Redis apna seconds + microseconds deta hai, script usse milliseconds banata hai. Ek Redis = ek clock, toh saare instances same 'now' par agree karte hain.

Tests ke liye `now` inject hota hai (parity test ko time control karna hai). Test 'without a clock option the time argument is EMPTY' args `["1", "1", "", "1"]` vs `["1", "1", "1234", "1"]` check karta hai, aur mutation R4 (hamesha app clock bhejo) isi se pakdi gayi.
why_needed: Distributed system mein 'abhi kitne baje hain' ka ek hi source hona chahiye, warna har node apna alag sach banata hai.
real_world_analogy: Teen referees alag alag ghadi se match ka time count karein toh kabhi match lamba, kabhi chhota. Ek stadium clock sab dekhein toh jhagda khatam.
how_it_works: Redis `TIME` command `[seconds, microseconds]` deta hai. Script `now = tonumber(t[1]) * 1000 + math.floor(tonumber(t[2]) / 1000)` se ms banata hai. Store ARGV ko `[...algorithm.args(), now, String(cost)]` banata hai, toh ARGV[3] time hai aur ARGV[4] cost.
in_this_project: `src/redis-store.ts` mein `RedisStoreOptions.now` aur `RedisStore.consume`; dono Lua scripts mein `ARGV[3] == ''` branch. `test/redis.test.ts` mein 'uses Redis's own clock by default' aur 'without a clock option the time argument is EMPTY' tests. README: 'app servers whose clocks drift still agree; the store sends an empty time argument for that (tested)'.

Tests ke liye clock inject ho sakti hai
Koi extra round trip nahi -- TIME script ke andar hi hai
disadvantages: Redis ki clock khud jump kare (VM pause, NTP step) toh sabko same galat time dikhega
Do alag Redis (jaise cluster ke nodes) ki clocks phir bhi alag ho sakti hain
common_mistakes: App ka `Date.now()` bhej dena 'kyunki NTP hai'
Clock backwards jaane par refill negative hone dena (`max(now - ts, 0)` bhool jaana)
Test clock production mein bhi pass kar dena

question: With several app instances, what limit does a MemoryStore actually enforce compared with a RedisStore, and what evidence does this project have for both?
answer_hinglish:
MemoryStore har process ki apni `Map` hai. N instances = N alag counters, toh ek client effectively N x limit tak le sakta hai (load balancer ke spread par depend karta hai). RedisStore mein saare instances ek hi key par ek hi Lua script chalate hain, toh limit exactly limit hai.

Evidence teen level par hai. Pehla, deterministic test `test/express.test.ts` 'two Express instances sharing one Redis': do real Express apps, har ek ka apna ioredis client, sliding window `limit: 10, windowMs: 60_000`, key hamesha 'shared-client', 30 requests dono instances par concurrently -> exactly 10 x 200 aur 20 x 429. Yeh har `npm test` mein chalta hai (Redis ho toh).

Doosra, load test `bench/load.mjs`: 3 Express instances alag Node processes mein, 32 concurrent connections round-robin, ek shared key, sliding window limit 500 per 10 minute. Run 1 (Windows 11, Ryzen 5 4500, Redis Docker mein same PC par): `redis-shared` -> exactly 500 allowed, 503 denied, kuch aur status nahi. Same setup `memory-shared` -> 1116 allowed, 0 denied. 1116 > 500 -- 'N instances, up to N x the limit' measured. 1500 tak nahi pahuncha kyunki har instance ko apne 500 tak pahunchne layak requests hi nahi mili.

Teesra, honesty: run 2 mein PC slow tha, shared key ko 3 second mein sirf 410 requests gayi, toh limit tak pahuncha hi nahi -- README kehta hai yeh cap ke baare mein kuch prove nahi karta; uska memory run (956 allowed, 0 denied) bhi kisi per-instance limit tak nahi pahuncha. Throughput numbers bhi valid nahi maane gaye (CPU 90-100% busy tha), toh main sirf correctness claim karta hoon.
why_needed: Interview mein 'Redis kyun' ka jawab sirf theory nahi, measured evidence se dena strong hota hai -- aur yeh bhi batana ki kaunsa run kuch prove nahi karta.
real_world_analogy: Teen darwaze, har ek ka apna register: har darwaze par guard 500 gin ke rokta hai, toh total 1500 andar aa sakte hain. Ek shared register (Redis) ho toh total 500.
how_it_works: MemoryStore: `algorithm.step(this.entries.get(key), this.now(), cost)` -- sirf local state. RedisStore: `evalsha` -> ek shared key `rl:...` par atomic script. Load test mein `mode === "memory-shared"` aur `"redis-shared"` dono `slidingWindow({ limit: LIMIT, windowMs: 600_000 })` aur `key: () => "shared"` use karte hain; sirf store alag hai.
in_this_project: `test/express.test.ts` (describe 'two Express instances sharing one Redis'), `bench/load.mjs` (correctness loop), raw results `bench/reference-results/2026-11-23-win32-load-run1.json` (`allowed: 500, denied: 503`; memory `allowed: 1116`) aur `-run2.json` (`allowed: 410, denied: 0`). `src/memory-store.ts` ka comment: 'N instances -> up to N x the limit'.

MemoryStore: zero network, single instance ya dev ke liye sahi
Dono same algorithm code share karte hain (parity tested)
disadvantages: Redis: har request par ek network round trip aur ek shared dependency
MemoryStore: autoscaling ke saath effective limit badalti rehti hai
common_mistakes: 3 instances par MemoryStore lagake socha 'limit 100 hai'
Load test ke run 2 (410 requests) ko bhi 'Redis held the limit' ka proof bolna
Busy machine ke throughput numbers ko result maanna
follow_up_questions: Sticky sessions se MemoryStore kaafi ho jayega kya?
Run 2 ko kaise valid banate?
Instances ko limit/N dena kab theek hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Redis correctness deta hai par ek network hop aur ek dependency add karta hai; MemoryStore free hai par limit replicas ke saath scale hoti hai. Isliye design mein dono hain, aur FailoverStore Redis down hone par memory par girta hai (degraded, per instance).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Redis down: shared limit gayi -- FailoverStore ho toh har instance apni MemoryStore se limit karta hai (N x limit), na ho toh onStoreError decide karta hai. Load balancer uneven spread kare toh MemoryStore ka effective limit unpredictable hota hai.
advanced.alternatives: Har instance ko limit/N dena (Redis nahi chahiye, par autoscaling par galat), sticky routing per client (failover par reset), gossip-based counters (PLAN ke 'Not in scope' mein).

Is repo mein woh measure nahi hua.

question: Why use a Lua script for atomicity instead of MULTI/EXEC, WATCH with optimistic retries, or a plain INCR plus EXPIRE?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki rate limiter ko 'padho, phir uske basis par decide karo, phir likho' chahiye -- aur in teeno alternatives mein se sirf Lua yeh ek round trip mein, bina retry ke karta hai.

MULTI/EXEC: commands queue hote hain aur saath execute hote hain, lekin queue karte waqt tumhe pichle command ka result nahi milta. Token bucket ko pehle tokens padhne hain, phir refill calculate karna hai, phir `tokens >= cost` par branch karna hai. MULTI ke andar branch nahi ho sakta, toh read MULTI ke bahar karna padega -- aur wahi race wapas aa gaya.

WATCH + MULTI (optimistic locking): key WATCH karo, GET karo, decide karo, MULTI/EXEC. Agar beech mein kisi ne key badli toh EXEC null deta hai aur retry karo. Kaam karta hai, par hot key par (ek popular user ya ek shared key) contention mein retries ka storm aata hai -- 300 concurrent requests mein bahut saare baar baar fail honge. Aur har attempt multiple round trips hai.

INCR + EXPIRE: fixed window ke liye theek, par yeh do commands hain (INCR ke baad crash ho toh EXPIRE kabhi nahi lagta -- key forever), aur token bucket ka fractional refill ya sliding window ka weighted estimate INCR se nahi banta. Plus 'denied request count mat karo' -- INCR pehle hi count kar deta hai.

Lua mein yeh sab ek script hai: `sliding_counter.lua` dono GET, estimate, aur sirf allow hone par `INCRBY` + `PEXPIRE` -- deny path pehle hi `return` kar deta hai. Cost yeh hai ki script ke dauraan Redis kuch aur nahi chalata, isliye scripts O(1) hain: 2-4 commands, koi loop nahi. Project 1 ke scripts reuse kiye gaye hain kyunki woh wahan 3 replicas ke saath tested the (PLAN).
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki tum Redis ke atomicity tools ka farak samajhte ho, sirf 'Lua use kiya' nahi.
real_world_analogy: MULTI ek sealed envelope mein instructions bhejna hai -- beech mein jawab dekh ke plan nahi badal sakte. WATCH ek 'agar kisi ne chheda toh dobara try karo' wala tareeka hai. Lua ek trusted aadmi ko andar bhejna hai jo khud dekh ke, decide karke, kaam karke wapas aata hai, aur jab tak woh andar hai darwaza band.
how_it_works: Redis script ke saare `redis.call` ek atomic unit mein chalate hain. Script ke andar conditionals, arithmetic aur multiple keys allowed hain. Script ka body ek baar `SCRIPT LOAD` hota hai aur phir `EVALSHA` sirf SHA bhejta hai.
in_this_project: `src/lua/sliding_counter.lua`: `GET cur_key`, `GET prev_key`, `estimated = cur + prev * weight`, deny par turant `return {0, ...}` (koi write nahi), allow par `INCRBY` aur `PEXPIRE cur_key window * 2`. `src/lua/token_bucket.lua`: `HMGET` -> refill -> decide -> `HSET` + `PEXPIRE`. Mutation U2 (Lua: denied request still counted in the sliding window) real-Redis tests se pakdi gayi.
code_example:
-- real, src/lua/sliding_counter.lua (trimmed)
local cur = tonumber(redis.call('GET', cur_key) or '0')
local prev = tonumber(redis.call('GET', prev_key) or '0')
local estimated = cur + prev * weight
if estimated + cost > limit then
  -- ... retry calculation ...
  return {0, math.max(math.floor(limit - estimated), 0), math.max(retry, 1), window - elapsed}
end
cur = redis.call('INCRBY', cur_key, cost)
redis.call('PEXPIRE', cur_key, window * 2)

Conditional logic server-side, atomic
Hot key par bhi contention retries nahi

Logic Lua mein hai -- debugging aur testing mushkil, isliye parity test
Redis Cluster mein saari keys same slot mein honi chahiye

question: How do the Redis keys of this rate limiter get cleaned up, and why are the expiry values capacity/rate + 1 s for the token bucket and 2 x window for the sliding window?
answer_hinglish:
Redis keys `PEXPIRE` se khud expire hoti hain -- koi cleanup job nahi hai. Values aisi chuni gayi hain ki key tab hi mitti hai jab uska hona ya na hona decision par koi farak nahi daalta.

Token bucket: `PEXPIRE KEYS[1], math.ceil(capacity * 1000 / rate) + 1000`. Ek khaali bucket `capacity / rate` seconds mein poora refill ho jaata hai. Us ke baad stored state 'full bucket' hai -- aur nayi key bhi full bucket se start hoti hai (`tokens = capacity`). Toh us time ke baad key delete karna decision nahi badalta. +1 second safety margin hai. Har request (deny bhi) `HSET` aur `PEXPIRE` karti hai, toh active client ki key zinda rehti hai. Example: capacity 2, rate 1 -> 2000 + 1000 = 3000 ms, aur test 'uses Redis's own clock by default ... sets an expiry on the key' check karta hai `pttl > 0` aur `<= 3000`.

Sliding window: har window ki apni key hai `<base>:<window start>`. Current window ki key ki zaroorat agle window mein bhi hai -- tab woh 'previous' ban jaati hai aur weighted count deti hai. Uske baad (do windows peeche) woh kabhi count nahi hoti. Isliye `PEXPIRE cur_key, window * 2`. Yeh sirf allowed path par lagta hai, `INCRBY` ke saath -- denied request kuch likhti hi nahi.

Kyun zaroori? Keys clients se aati hain (IP, email). Bina expiry ke har ek-baar aaya IP Redis memory mein hamesha rahega. Mutation U3 (Lua: no expiry on the token bucket key) isi test se pakdi gayi.
why_needed: Rate-limit keys ki sankhya attacker control kar sakta hai; expiry na ho toh Redis memory dheere dheere bhar jaati hai.
real_world_analogy: Gym ka visitor register: jo 30 din se nahi aaya uska page phaad do -- kyunki agar woh wapas aaya toh naye member jaisa hi treat hoga, toh purana page rakhne ka koi fayda nahi.
how_it_works: `PEXPIRE key ms` key par millisecond TTL lagata hai; Redis expired keys ko lazily (access par) aur background sampling se hatata hai. Script har write ke baad TTL refresh karta hai, toh TTL 'last activity se' count hota hai.
in_this_project: `src/lua/token_bucket.lua` line: `redis.call('PEXPIRE', KEYS[1], math.ceil(capacity * 1000 / rate) + 1000)`. `src/lua/sliding_counter.lua`: `redis.call('PEXPIRE', cur_key, window * 2)`. TypeScript MemoryStore mein koi per-key expiry nahi hai -- mutation M3 ne dikhaya ki woh koi decision nahi badalti thi, isliye hata di; memory `maxKeys` (LRU) se bounded hai. Test: `test/redis.test.ts` 'uses Redis's own clock by default (no now passed): works and sets an expiry on the key'.

-- real, src/lua/token_bucket.lua

-- real, src/lua/sliding_counter.lua
-- Keep it for 2 windows: it is needed as "previous" during the next window.
redis.call('PEXPIRE', cur_key, window * 2)

question: Would this rate limiter work on Redis Cluster? Explain the undeclared-keys problem in the sliding window script and how you would fix it.
answer_hinglish:
Seedha jawab: Redis Cluster par yeh TESTED nahi hai, aur sliding window script mein ek known problem hai. README isko 'NOT implemented' mein clearly likhta hai.

Cluster mein har key ek hash slot (16384 mein se ek) mein jaati hai aur har slot ek node par hai. Script ko jo keys `KEYS` mein di jaati hain, client unhi se decide karta hai ki script kis node par bhejna hai. Token bucket theek hai: ek hi key `KEYS[1]` per client.

Sliding window `KEYS[1]` sirf base key leta hai, aur andar do keys BANATA hai: `cur_key = KEYS[1] .. ':' .. cur_start` aur `prev_key`. Yeh KEYS mein declared nahi hain. Inka slot base key se alag ho sakta hai -- tab woh doosre node par hongi aur Redis non-local key access refuse kar deta hai. Aur declared keys ka rule Redis ka official contract bhi hai.

Fix kyun simple nahi? Keys declare karne ke liye app ko `cur_start` pehle pata hona chahiye -- yani app ka clock. Lekin default design Redis TIME use karta hai taaki drift na ho. Declare karna = app clock wapas lana. Trade-off.

Practical fix: hash tag. Cluster sirf `{...}` ke andar ka hissa hash karta hai. Key `rl:login:{email:a@b.com}` ho toh `rl:login:{email:a@b.com}:1700000000000` bhi same slot mein jaayegi. Toh base key mein client id ko braces mein daal do -- teeno keys ek slot, ek node. Yeh bhi is repo mein 'not done or tested' hai. Production mein main pehle cluster par yeh test likhta (dono algorithms, keys ka slot check), phir hash-tag key helper. Dhyan: hash tag ka matlab ek client ki saari keys ek node par -- woh theek hai, kyunki yahi chahiye.
why_needed: Scale par Redis Cluster common hai; 'Lua atomic hai' bolne ke baad interviewer zaroor poochta hai ki multi-key script cluster mein kaise chalega.
real_world_analogy: Ek library ki multiple branches hain aur har book ki branch uske title ke pehle letter se tay hoti hai. Agar ek kaam ke liye teen books chahiye jinke title alag letters se shuru hote hain, toh ek branch mein sab nahi milengi. Hash tag yeh hai ki teeno ke title par ek hi sticker lagao jisse branch tay ho.
how_it_works: Slot = CRC16(key) mod 16384, aur agar key mein `{...}` hai toh sirf braces ke andar ka text hash hota hai. Script ki saari keys ek slot mein honi chahiye; declared KEYS se client routing karta hai aur Redis cross-slot access par error deta hai.
in_this_project: `src/lua/sliding_counter.lua` mein `local cur_key = KEYS[1] .. ':' .. cur_start` aur `local prev_key = KEYS[1] .. ':' .. prev_start`. `src/redis-store.ts` `evalsha(sha, [key], args)` sirf ek key bhejta hai. `src/limiter.ts` key ko `this.prefix + key` banata hai -- hash tag ka koi handling nahi. README 'NOT implemented': 'Redis Cluster: NOT tested ... A hash tag in the key (e.g. {user42}) would keep them together -- not done or tested here.'

Redis TIME wala design bacha rehta hai
disadvantages: Abhi kuch tested nahi hai
Hash tag user ki responsibility hai -- bhool gaye toh cluster mein error
Galat hash tag (jaise poora prefix braces mein) saare clients ko ek slot/node par daal deta hai -- hot node
common_mistakes: Script ke andar keys banana aur sochna cluster mein chalega
`{rl}` jaisa constant hash tag lagana -- sab ek node par
Single-node Redis par test pass hone ko cluster support maan lena

Hash tag se hot slot problem kab aati hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Option 1: hash tag in key (script unchanged, Redis TIME bacha, par user ko braces lagane hain). Option 2: app cur/prev keys calculate karke KEYS mein bheje (contract-correct, par app clock wapas -- drift ka problem). Option 3: sliding window ko ek hash key mein rakho (fields = window start) -- script badalna padega aur project 1 ke tested script se divergence.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Hash tag ke bina: cross-slot error har request par -> store error -> onStoreError/FailoverStore. Cluster resharding ke dauraan MOVED/ASK redirects -- RedisStore unhe NOSCRIPT ki tarah retry nahi karta, client (ioredis Cluster) ko handle karna hoga; tested nahi.
advanced.alternatives: Redis Cluster ki jagah sharded single-node Redis instances with client-side consistent hashing; ya ek dedicated rate-limit service; ya per-region Redis.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x par ek Redis node kaafi ho sakta hai (O(1) scripts); 100x par cluster ya sharding zaroori. Tab hash tags ka per-client distribution hi load spread karega -- isliye tag mein client id ho, constant nahi.
advanced.production_improvements: Ek `clusterSafeKey(id)` helper jo braces lagaye aur id ke andar ke braces escape/reject kare, ek real Redis Cluster (docker) par test suite, aur RateLimiter mein validation jo cluster mode mein bina hash tag ki key reject kare.

question: Redis replication is asynchronous. What happens to rate-limit state when the Redis primary fails over to a replica, and what in this code helps or does not help?
answer_hinglish:
Seedha: kuch recent counts kho sakte hain, aur limit kuch time ke liye thodi loose ho sakti hai. Rate limiter ke liye yeh usually acceptable hai, par interview mein yeh bolna zaroori hai ki 'exactly 50' guarantee single Redis primary ke andar hai, failover ke across nahi.

Kyun? Primary write acknowledge karta hai aur replica ko baad mein bhejta hai. Agar primary crash ho jaye aur last kuch writes replica tak na pahunche, toh promoted replica purana state dekhega: token bucket mein zyada tokens, sliding window mein kam count. Clients ko kuch extra requests mil jaati hain -- over-allow, under-allow nahi.

Is code mein kya help karta hai? Pehla, NOSCRIPT handling: naye primary ke paas script cache nahi ho sakta (Redis script cache persist/replicate hone ki guarantee nahi), toh `EVALSHA` NOSCRIPT dega; `RedisStore` script load karke ek baar retry karta hai. README failover ko NOSCRIPT ke reasons mein list karta hai. Doosra, Redis TIME: naye primary ka apna clock hai; agar woh pichle primary se alag ho toh `ts` ke against `elapsed` thoda galat -- token bucket ka `math.max(now - ts, 0)` backwards jump par tokens add nahi karta. Teesra, transition ke dauraan errors (connection reset, READONLY agar client abhi bhi purane node par likhe) store se throw hote hain -- `FailoverStore` + MemoryStore fallback ho toh decisions degraded par limited rehte hain.

Kya help nahi karta: lost counts recover karne ka koi mechanism nahi, aur failover scenario actually test nahi hua -- sirf `SCRIPT FLUSH` (NOSCRIPT) aur ek fake READONLY error test hue hain. Security limits (login) ke liye main `WAIT` jaisa synchronous replication sochta, latency ki keemat par -- yeh implement nahi hai.
why_needed: Senior interviewer guarantees ki boundary poochta hai: 'exactly N' kis condition mein true hai aur kab nahi.
real_world_analogy: Bank ka main branch apni ledger copy shaam ko doosri branch bhejta hai. Main branch dopahar mein jal jaye toh backup branch ki ledger mein subah tak ke hi entries hain -- kuch withdrawals ka record nahi, toh customer ko lagta hai paise zyada hain.
how_it_works: Redis async replication: primary client ko OK pehle bhejta hai, replication stream baad mein. Sentinel/Cluster failover replica ko primary banata hai. Script cache par bharosa nahi kiya ja sakta: restart ke baad khaali hota hai, aur failover ke baad naye primary par script ho bhi sakta hai, nahi bhi -- isliye NOSCRIPT handling zaroori hai.
in_this_project: `src/redis-store.ts` ka comment: 'If Redis does not know the script (restart, SCRIPT FLUSH, failover), it gets NOSCRIPT; the store loads the script and retries once.' `src/lua/token_bucket.lua` mein `math.max(now - ts, 0)`. `src/failover-store.ts` ka `FailoverStore` transition errors ko fallback par bhejta hai. Test sirf `admin.script("FLUSH")` aur ek fake `READONLY` error se hain, real failover nahi.
advantages: Failover ke baad NOSCRIPT apne aap recover
Over-allow hi hota hai, legit users block nahi hote
Fallback ke saath transition window mein bhi limit rehti hai
disadvantages: Lost counts ka koi recovery nahi
Real failover test nahi hua
Security limits ke liye brief loose window risk hai
common_mistakes: 'Lua atomic hai toh kabhi limit nahi tootegi' bolna -- atomicity aur durability alag cheezein hain
Script cache ko persistent maan lena
Har failover error ko retry karna (READONLY par retry purane node par hi jaata hai)
follow_up_questions: WAIT command latency ko kitna badhayega?
Sentinel vs Cluster failover mein client ka behaviour kaise alag hai?
Rate limiter ke liye AOF fsync always kabhi justified hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Rate limiting mein speed aur availability ke liye async replication aur kabhi kabhi over-allow accept kiya jaata hai; strong durability (WAIT, fsync always) har request ki latency badhati hai. Capacity limits ke liye loose theek, security limits ke liye sochna padta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Primary crash: last writes lost -> extra allowance. Split brain (do primaries thodi der): do alag counters -> limit roughly double us dauraan. Script cache missing: NOSCRIPT -> reload. Client purane primary se juda: READONLY -> error, retry nahi.
advanced.alternatives: Synchronous replication via WAIT (Redis mein partial), per-region independent limits, ya ek consensus-based store (etcd jaisa) -- rate limiting ke liye usually bahut mehenga.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada traffic par failover ke dauraan lost writes ki sankhya bhi badhti hai (same time window mein zyada writes). 100x par cluster ke multiple primaries hain; har ek ka failover independent hai, toh har shard ki keys alag time par loose hoti hain.
advanced.production_improvements: Failover drill likho (docker Sentinel ke saath) jo check kare: NOSCRIPT recover hua, errors fallback par gaye, extra allowance kitna tha. Store errors aur degraded decisions ka metric aur alert. Login jaise limits ke liye fail-closed (`onStoreError: "deny"`) already available hai.

question: Walk through RedisStore.consume: how is the script SHA computed and cached, why EVALSHA instead of EVAL, and what does the SHA-mismatch check protect against?
answer_hinglish:
`RedisStore.consume` teen kaam karta hai: script ka SHA lo, `EVALSHA` chalao, aur NOSCRIPT par ek baar load karke retry karo.

SHA: module-level `scripts` Map hai. `load(file)` pehli baar Lua file `readFileSync(new URL(`./lua/${file}`, import.meta.url))` se padhta hai aur `createHash("sha1").update(source).digest("hex")` se SHA1 nikalta hai -- yahi Redis bhi script ke liye calculate karta hai. Phir Map mein cache, toh file har request par nahi padhi jaati. `import.meta.url` relative path isliye ki build ke baad `scripts/copy-lua.mjs` Lua files ko `dist/` mein JS ke paas copy karta hai.

EVALSHA kyun? `EVAL` har request par poora script body bhejta hai -- har call par extra bytes aur Redis ko har baar hash karna. `EVALSHA` sirf 40-character SHA bhejta hai. PLAN kehta hai: 'the script body is sent once per Redis restart, not on every request'.

Flow: `evalsha(sha, [key], args)`. Error aaye toh message mein 'NOSCRIPT' check -- nahi hai toh `throw error` (koi retry nahi). Hai toh `scriptLoad(source)`, aur jo SHA Redis ne return kiya usse local `sha` se compare: `if (loaded !== sha) throw new Error(`script SHA mismatch ...`)`. Yeh guard karta hai ki hum jis SHA ko call karenge woh sach mein loaded script hai -- warna retry phir NOSCRIPT deta, ya kisi encoding/line-ending farak (jaise file alag tarah padhi gayi) ki wajah se galat assumption chhupi rehti. Phir ek baar `evalsha` retry. Result `toDecision` mein validate hota hai.

Mutations R1 (NOSCRIPT not handled -> 2 tests fail) aur R2 (every error retried -> 1 test fails) yeh flow guard karte hain.
why_needed: Per-request overhead aur restart-resilience dono ek saath -- yeh EVALSHA pattern almost har production Redis-Lua code mein hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant mein regular customer 'number 7' bolta hai, poori recipe nahi. Naya cook (Redis restart) '7 kya hai?' pooche toh customer ek baar recipe de deta hai, aur phir se '7' bolta hai.
how_it_works: Redis script cache SHA1(body) se index karta hai. `SCRIPT LOAD` body store karke SHA return karta hai; `EVALSHA sha numkeys keys... args...` cache se chalata hai, na mile toh `NOSCRIPT No matching script` error.
in_this_project: `src/redis-store.ts`: `const scripts = new Map<string, { source: string; sha: string }>()`, function `load`, class `RedisStore` ka `consume`. Test 'NOSCRIPT after SCRIPT FLUSH (e.g. a Redis restart): loads the script and carries on' real Redis par `SCRIPT FLUSH` karke check karta hai ki agla call `{ allowed: true, remaining: 1 }` deta hai.

Restart/flush/failover ke baad apne aap recover
SHA mismatch silently ignore nahi hota
disadvantages: Pehli request restart ke baad do extra round trips leti hai
NOSCRIPT detection error message ke string par depend karta hai
common_mistakes: Har request par EVAL use karna
NOSCRIPT par infinite retry loop
SHA hardcode karna aur script badalne par update bhoolna

question: How do the arguments reach the Lua script? Explain the KEYS/ARGV layout and what the ioredisClient adapter does.
answer_hinglish:
Redis script ko do arrays milte hain: `KEYS` (jin keys ko script chhoota hai) aur `ARGV` (baaki values, sab strings). Is project mein dono scripts ka layout same hai: `KEYS[1]` = client ki key (prefix ke saath, jaise `rl:login:email:a@b.com`), `ARGV[1]` aur `ARGV[2]` = algorithm ke numbers, `ARGV[3]` = now (ya empty), `ARGV[4]` = cost.

TypeScript side: har algorithm ek `args()` deta hai -- token bucket `[String(capacity), String(rate)]`, sliding window `[String(limit), String(window)]`. `RedisStore.consume` usme do aur jodta hai: `const args = [...algorithm.args(), now, String(cost)]`. Lua side har cheez `tonumber` se number banata hai. Sab string kyun? Redis protocol mein arguments bulk strings hi hote hain.

`ioredisClient` ek chhota adapter hai. Store ka apna interface `RedisScriptClient` hai: `evalsha(sha, keys, args)` aur `scriptLoad(script)`. ioredis ka signature alag hai: `evalsha(sha, numKeys, ...keysAndArgs)` aur `script("LOAD", body)`. Adapter translate karta hai: `client.evalsha(sha, keys.length, ...keys, ...args)` -- `numKeys` Redis ko batata hai ki pehle kitne arguments keys hain. Aur `String(await client.script("LOAD", script))`.

Adapter structural hai -- ioredis import nahi karta, sirf shape maangta hai. Isliye package ki koi runtime dependency nahi. Test 'without a clock option the time argument is EMPTY' exact args check karta hai: `["1", "1", "", "1"]`.
why_needed: KEYS aur ARGV ka sahi istemal cluster routing aur script correctness dono ke liye zaroori hai; aur adapter pattern se library kisi bhi client ke saath chalti hai.
real_world_analogy: Courier form: 'kis address par' (KEYS) alag box mein, 'kya bhejna hai' (ARGV) alag box mein. Adapter ek translator hai jo tumhara form courier company ke format mein bhar deta hai.
how_it_works: `EVALSHA sha 1 rl:x 5 3 '' 1` -- yahan `1` numkeys hai, `rl:x` KEYS[1], baaki ARGV[1..4]. Lua arrays 1-indexed hain.
in_this_project: `src/algorithms.ts` mein `args: () => [String(capacity), String(rate)]`; `src/redis-store.ts` mein `RedisScriptClient`, `ioredisClient`, aur `consume` ka `args` array; Lua header comments: `-- ARGV[1] = capacity, ARGV[2] = refill_per_sec, ARGV[3] = now_ms ('' => Redis TIME), ARGV[4] = cost`.
advantages: Do methods ka interface -- koi bhi Redis client fit ho jaata hai
Koi runtime dependency nahi
ARGV layout dono scripts mein same
disadvantages: Positional ARGV -- order galat toh silently galat numbers
Sab strings, toh number formatting (String(0.001)) par bharosa
common_mistakes: Keys ko ARGV mein bhejna (cluster routing toot jaati hai)
`numKeys` galat dena
Lua mein 0-indexed array samajhna

Lua mein `tonumber('')` kya deta hai?

question: What is luaToString, and why does the TypeScript token bucket store a rounded token count but reply from the full-precision value?
answer_hinglish:
Redis ka Lua jab ek number ko `tostring()` se string banata hai, toh `%.14g` format use karta hai -- sirf 14 significant digits. Token bucket fractional tokens store karta hai (`HSET ... 'tokens', tostring(tokens)`), toh Redis mein jo value jaati hai woh 14 digits par rounded hoti hai. JavaScript ka number ~17 digits rakhta hai. Agar memory store full precision rakhe aur Redis 14 digits, toh hazaaron steps baad dono ke tokens thode alag honge, aur kisi boundary par ek allow karega aur doosra deny.

Isliye `luaToString = (x) => Number(x.toPrecision(14))` -- exactly wahi rounding. Test: `luaToString(1 / 3)` -> `0.33333333333333`, `luaToString(4.999999999999999)` -> `5`.

Ab subtle part. Lua script mein `tokens` variable full precision hai; `tostring` sirf HSET ke waqt string banata hai. Reply -- `math.floor(tokens)` aur `reset = math.ceil((capacity - tokens) * 1000 / rate)` -- usi full-precision variable se banta hai. Pehle TypeScript version ne pehle round kiya aur phir rounded value se reply banaya. Parity test seed 1 ke step 91 par fail hua: `resetMs` 1135 vs 1136. `ceil` ke saath ek chhota sa farak (14th digit) ek poora millisecond ban gaya.

Fix: `step()` reply full value se banata hai aur sirf return kiye gaye `state` mein `luaToString(tokens)` lagata hai. Code comment: 'The reply uses the FULL-precision value (the Lua variable); only the STORED value is rounded by tostring().' Mutation L1 (store full precision) parity test fail karta hai -- toh rounding bhi necessary hai, sirf decorative nahi.

Ek aur detail: Lua file ka purana comment 'Store state with full precision (tostring keeps the fraction)' imprecise hai -- file ke top par ab ek note hai ki `tostring` 14 significant digits (`%.14g`) rakhta hai; script ka code project 1 se unchanged hai.
why_needed: Do implementations 'same' tabhi hain jab woh floating point tak same hon. Yeh question dikhata hai ki tumne sach mein dono ko bit-level par compare kiya.
real_world_analogy: Do accountants same hisaab rakhte hain, ek 14 decimal tak likhta hai aur doosra 17 tak. Mahino baad kisi din ek ka total 1135 aata hai aur doosre ka 1136 -- aur ek customer ko refund milta hai, doosre ko nahi.
how_it_works: Lua 5.1 (Redis) `tostring(number)` = `string.format('%.14g', n)`. `toPrecision(14)` JavaScript mein same significant-digit rounding deta hai, aur `Number(...)` wapas number banata hai. State rounded, reply full.
in_this_project: `src/algorithms.ts::luaToString` aur `tokenBucket` ka `step`: `resetMs: Math.ceil(((capacity - tokens) * 1000) / rate)` full `tokens` se, phir `return { state: { tokens: luaToString(tokens), ts: now }, decision }`. `test/algorithms.test.ts` mein `describe("luaToString")`. README section 'Parity: the TypeScript and the Lua versions must agree'.

Bug ka exact cause code comment mein documented
disadvantages: Redis ke Lua version ki implementation detail par depend karta hai -- Redis ka Lua badle toh parity test hi pakdega
Code reader ko surprise lagta hai ki rounding kyun
common_mistakes: Float comparison ko 'close enough' maan lena
State aur reply dono ek jaise round karna
Lua ke `tostring` ko lossless samajhna
follow_up_questions: Tokens ko integer milli-tokens mein store karte toh yeh problem hoti?
Parity test ne step 91 tak yeh kyun nahi pakda?
Redis Lua ke saath aur kaunse numeric gotchas hain (jaise reply mein float truncation)?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Do implementations rakhne ka cost yahi hai: har numeric detail match karni padti hai. Alternative ek hi implementation (sirf Lua) hai, par tab memory store ko bhi Redis chahiye ya ek Lua interpreter. Project ne duplication + parity test chuna.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Redis ka Lua runtime ya number formatting kabhi badle toh memory aur Redis decisions diverge karenge -- sirf parity test (real Redis ke saath) pakdega, isliye CI mein Redis zaroori hai.
advanced.alternatives: Integer arithmetic (milli-tokens) se float ka problem khatam hota, par project 1 ka Lua script badalna padta -- jo 'unchanged reuse' decision ke against hai.

question: Why does RedisStore check the shape of the script's reply, and why does every value the Lua scripts return go through math.floor or math.ceil?
answer_hinglish:
`toDecision` check karta hai ki reply exactly 4 numbers ka array hai: `[allowed, remaining, retry, reset]`. Kuch aur aaya -- `null`, string, 2 elements -- toh `throw new Error(`unexpected reply from the rate-limit script: ...`)`. README: 'An unexpected reply shape is an error, never a guessed decision.'

Kyun? Rate limiter ka sabse khatarnak bug silent hota hai. Agar code `raw[0] === 1` blindly padhe aur reply galat shape ka ho (koi aur script same SHA naam se nahi ho sakta, par galat client adapter, RESP3 mapping, ya script edit ho sakta hai), toh `undefined === 1` false -> sab deny; ya kisi aur mapping mein sab allow. Error throw karne se problem turant dikhti hai aur onStoreError/FailoverStore ka path chalta hai, jo explicit decision hai. Test 'an unexpected reply shape is an error, not a guess' fake client `[1, 2]` return karta hai; mutation R3 (reply shape not checked) isi se pakdi gayi.

Ab floor/ceil. Redis jab Lua number ko reply mein convert karta hai toh use INTEGER reply banata hai -- fraction truncate ho jaata hai. Agar script `tokens` (jaise 2.7) seedha return kare toh client ko 2 milega, aur yeh rounding direction implicit hogi. Isliye script khud explicit karta hai: `math.floor(tokens)` remaining ke liye (2.7 token = 2 poori requests), `math.ceil(...)` retry aur reset ke liye (time hamesha upar round -- jaldi retry karna fail hoga). Isi wajah se `typeof x === "number"` check bhi kaam karta hai: ioredis integer replies ko JS numbers deta hai.

TypeScript `step()` bhi same floor/ceil karta hai, warna parity toot jaati. Mutation L5 (retry rounded down) yeh guard karta hai.
why_needed: Boundary par validation (network/external system se aaya data) ek general engineering principle hai; Lua-Redis number conversion ek specific gotcha hai jo interviewers poochte hain.
real_world_analogy: Bank ATM agar 'balance' field mein kuch ajeeb (khaali ya text) paye toh paise dene ya mana karne ki jagah 'service unavailable' dikhata hai -- guess nahi karta.
how_it_works: Lua number -> Redis integer reply (truncate towards zero); Lua table -> array reply; Lua `false` -> nil. `toDecision` `Array.isArray(raw) && raw.length === 4 && raw.every(x => typeof x === "number")` check karta hai, phir `allowed === 1` se boolean.
in_this_project: `src/redis-store.ts::toDecision`. Lua returns: `token_bucket.lua` -> `return {allowed, math.floor(tokens), retry, reset}` jahan `retry` aur `reset` `math.ceil` se bane hain; `sliding_counter.lua` -> `math.max(math.floor(limit - estimated), 0)`, `math.max(retry, 1)`. Test `test/redis.test.ts` 'an unexpected reply shape is an error, not a guess'.

Rounding direction explicit aur dono implementations mein same
Error message mein actual reply hai -- debugging aasaan
disadvantages: Reply format change karna ho toh TS aur Lua dono badalne padte hain
Check sirf shape ka hai, values ki range ka nahi
common_mistakes: Lua se float return karke expect karna ki client ko float milega
Reply ko `as any` karke padh lena
Retry time ko round down karna (client jaldi retry karke phir deny hoga)

`allowed` ko boolean ki jagah 1/0 kyun bheja?

question: Redis restarts in the middle of traffic. Walk through exactly what happens to requests on your three app instances, and what would happen if the retry also failed.
answer_hinglish:
Restart ke baad Redis ka script cache khaali hota hai, toh har instance ki agli `EVALSHA` NOSCRIPT error paayegi. Har instance independently recover karta hai: `RedisStore.consume` error message mein 'NOSCRIPT' dekhta hai, `scriptLoad(source)` karta hai, SHA compare karta hai, aur ek baar `evalsha` retry karta hai. User ko kuch nahi dikhta, bas us request par do extra round trips.

Teen instances par: teeno apna apna SCRIPT LOAD karenge -- koi coordination nahi chahiye kyunki SCRIPT LOAD idempotent hai (same body = same SHA). Ek hi instance par agar 20 requests ek saath NOSCRIPT paayein, toh code mein koi single-flight nahi hai -- 20 SCRIPT LOAD jaayenge. Woh correct hai (idempotent), bas thoda waste.

State ka kya? Agar Redis persistence (RDB/AOF) nahi hai toh saare counters gaye -- har client ko fresh limit. Rate limiter ke liye yeh over-allow hai, ek baar. Keys ke TTL chhote hain (bucket full time + 1 s, ya 2 windows), toh persistence ka fayda bhi limited hai.

Agar retry bhi fail ho? Code sirf EK retry karta hai. Retry ka error (connection refused, ya phir NOSCRIPT) seedha throw hota hai -- koi loop nahi. Woh error RateLimiter se upar jaata hai: FailoverStore ho toh `onError` call hota hai aur MemoryStore fallback degraded decision deta hai; nahi toh `StoreUnavailableError`, aur Express/Nest adapter ka `onStoreError` decide karta hai: 'error' (500 via error handler), 'allow' (fail open), ya 'deny' (503 + `Retry-After: 5`). Restart ke dauraan jab Redis abhi tak listen hi nahi kar raha, yahi path chalta hai.

question: RedisStore retries once on NOSCRIPT but passes every other error through, for example READONLY from a replica. Why is retrying those errors wrong?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki retry tabhi sense banata hai jab retry ke pehle tum cause fix kar sakte ho. NOSCRIPT ka cause pata hai aur fix tumhare haath mein hai: script load karo, phir same call kaam karega. Baaki errors ke saath aisa nahi.

READONLY ka matlab: tumhara connection ek replica par hai (jaise failover ke baad purana primary demote hua, aur client ne abhi topology refresh nahi ki). Usi connection par turant retry -> wahi replica -> phir READONLY. Sirf latency double hui aur Redis par load bhi. Agar code 'har error par SCRIPT LOAD + retry' kare (yahi mutation R2 hai: 'every error retried as if NOSCRIPT'), toh READONLY replica par SCRIPT LOAD bhi bhejega -- bekaar, aur failure chhupa ke slow bana deta hai.

Connection refused / timeout par bhi turant retry ka koi fayda nahi; Redis down hai toh 'retry storm' bas har request ko slow karta hai. Iske liye sahi jagah `FailoverStore` hai: guard (circuit breaker + timeout) aur fallback ek jagah. Circuit breaker dead Redis ko call karna hi band kar deta hai -- test mein 10 checks par dead store sirf 3 baar call hua.

To design yeh hai: `RedisStore` sirf apna specific, fixable case (NOSCRIPT) handle kare; baaki policy (retry, breaker, timeout, fallback) layer upar ho. Separation of concerns -- aur ek galat retry layer (store mein) aur ek sahi layer (failover) ek saath hone par retries multiply bhi ho jaate.

Test 'errors other than NOSCRIPT are passed through, not retried' ek fake client se `READONLY You can't write against a read only replica.` throw karta hai aur check karta hai `calls` exactly 1 hai aur error READONLY hi hai.
why_needed: Retry ek powerful tool hai jo galat jagah lage toh outage ko badha deta hai. Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki tum retryable vs non-retryable errors alag kar sakte ho.
real_world_analogy: Darwaza locked hai kyunki chabi galat thi (NOSCRIPT) -- sahi chabi lo aur ek baar phir kholo. Darwaza locked hai kyunki building hi band hai (READONLY, down) -- wahi darwaza 10 baar khatkhatane se kuch nahi hoga; doosra raasta (fallback) dhoondo.
how_it_works: `if (!String(err.message).includes("NOSCRIPT")) throw error;` -- non-NOSCRIPT errors turant upar. FailoverStore guard.execute(run) ke through breaker/timeout lagata hai aur catch mein fallback ya StoreUnavailableError.

Test `test/redis.test.ts` 'errors other than NOSCRIPT are passed through, not retried' (`expect(calls).toBe(1)`). `test/failover.test.ts` 'guarded by resilience-kit's circuit breaker: once open, the dead primary is not even called' (`expect(calls.n).toBe(3)`). question: Redis is completely unreachable. What do requests get with and without a FailoverStore, and why did the dead-Redis tests configure ioredis with enableOfflineQueue false and no retries?
answer_hinglish:
Teen layers decide karti hain. Pehli: client kaise fail hota hai. Doosri: FailoverStore hai ya nahi. Teesri: adapter ka `onStoreError`.

Bina FailoverStore ke: `RedisStore` ka error seedha adapter tak aata hai. Express adapter mein `onStoreError` -- default 'error' ka matlab `next(err)` (app ka error handler, test mein 500 'error handler'); 'allow' = fail open, request chalti hai bina `RateLimit-*` headers ke (test: 200, 200, 200 aur `ratelimit-limit` null); 'deny' = fail closed, 503 + `Retry-After: 5` + `{"error":"rate_limit_unavailable"}`. 503 kyunki problem server ki hai, client ki nahi.

FailoverStore + MemoryStore fallback ke saath: request MemoryStore se limit hoti hai, decision `degraded: true`. Test: capacity 2 -> 200, 200, 429 -- Redis down hai phir bhi limit hai, bas per instance.

Ab ioredis config. Test client: `new Redis("redis://127.0.0.1:1", { enableOfflineQueue: false, maxRetriesPerRequest: 0, retryStrategy: () => null, lazyConnect: true })`. Comment: 'offline queue off + no retries: commands fail at once instead of waiting for a reconnect'. ioredis ka default offline queue disconnected state mein commands ko queue karke reconnect ka wait karta hai -- yani request fail nahi hoti, HANG hoti hai. Production mein yahi sabse bura case hai: Redis down = har request latak gayi. Isliye README timeout guard ko important bolta hai: 'The timeout is what keeps a HANGING Redis ... from hanging every request' -- test mein ek kabhi-na-jawab-dene wala store 100 ms TimeoutPolicy ke baad fallback se answer deta hai.

Ek caveat: Redis call cancel nahi hoti (clients AbortSignal nahi lete), timeout sirf wait karna band karta hai.

Ek aur cheez jo code se dikhti hai: adapter 'allow'/'deny' ko har non-`RateLimitError` error par lagata hai, sirf `StoreUnavailableError` par nahi -- isliye bare RedisStore ka raw ECONNREFUSED bhi fail open/closed hota hai.
why_needed: Rate limiter khud ek dependency hai. Uske down hone par app ka behaviour pehle se decide hona chahiye, warna limiter hi outage ban jaata hai.
real_world_analogy: Security guard ka radio (Redis) band ho gaya. Option: (a) manager ko bulao (error), (b) sabko andar jaane do (fail open), (c) sabko roko (fail closed), (d) apni notebook se gino (memory fallback, sirf apne gate ke liye).
how_it_works: FailoverStore: `guard.execute(run)` -> error -> `onError` (throwing handler ignore) -> fallback ho toh `{ ...decision, degraded: true }`, warna `StoreUnavailableError` with cause. Adapter: `RateLimitError` hamesha throw; else mode 'error' throw, 'allow' next(), 'deny' 503.

Nest ke liye `test/nestjs.test.ts`: allow -> 200, deny -> 503, default -> 500.

question: Redis was down for a minute and the instances ran on their memory fallbacks. What is inconsistent when Redis comes back, and what are the subtle effects of a timed-out but still running Redis call?
answer_hinglish:
Do inconsistencies hain, aur dono README ke 'NOT implemented' mein honestly likhe hain.

Pehli: fallback ke counts Redis mein merge nahi hote. Degraded mode mein har instance ki MemoryStore ne apni requests gini. Redis wapas aaya toh Redis ke paas woh state hai jo outage se pehle thi (ya TTL se expire ho chuki). Toh ek client jisne outage mein instance A par apni poori limit use ki, Redis wapas aate hi phir se allowance pa sakta hai. Matlab outage + recovery ka total over-allowance: outage mein N x limit, plus recovery par Redis ka purana/khaali state. Capacity limit ke liye usually acceptable; brute-force sensitive limits ke liye login par `onStoreError: "deny"` ya fallback na rakhna better hai.

Doosri, subtle: timeout guard sirf WAIT karna band karta hai, call cancel nahi karta -- `RedisScriptClient` mein AbortSignal hai hi nahi, aur FailoverStore ka `run` signal use nahi karta. Socho Redis slow hai, call 50 ms timeout par chhoda, fallback ne decision diya. Lekin woh `EVALSHA` Redis tak pahunch chuka tha aur baad mein execute ho gaya -- token Redis mein bhi kharch ho gaya. Ek request, do jagah count: Redis mein bhi aur memory mein bhi. Is direction mein limit TIGHT hoti hai (under-allow), loose nahi. Aur slow Redis par aise pending calls jama hote hain jo recovery ke baad bhi execute hote rehte hain.

Teesra flap: circuit breaker half-open mein kuch requests Redis par aur kuch fallback par -- ek client ke decisions do alag states se aate hain.

Main yeh sab accept karunga capacity limits ke liye, aur interview mein clearly bolunga ki degraded mode 'best effort' hai; `degraded: true` flag isliye hai ki caller/metrics ko pata ho.
why_needed: Senior candidate se expect hota hai ki woh sirf failure nahi, recovery ke baad ki state bhi soche -- kaafi bugs 'Redis wapas aaya' ke baad hote hain.
real_world_analogy: Bank server ek ghante down tha, branches ne kagaz par withdrawals likhe. Server wapas aaya, kagaz ki entries feed nahi hui -- ab system ke hisaab se customers ke paas zyada paise hain. Aur ek cheque jo 'timeout' maan ke wapas kar diya tha, woh actually clear bhi ho gaya.
how_it_works: FailoverStore: `await (guard ? guard.execute(run) : run())` -- `run` ko signal pass nahi hota, toh underlying `evalsha` promise chalta rehta hai. Fallback ke decisions `degraded: true`. Koi reconciliation step nahi hai.

README 'NOT implemented': 'While degraded, the fallback's counts are per instance and are NOT merged back into Redis when it returns.' `src/types.ts`: `readonly degraded?: true`.

question: The parity test failed with 'step 91, seed 1': resetMs 1135 from TypeScript vs 1136 from Redis. How would you investigate this, what was the cause, and what was the fix?
answer_hinglish:
Symptom: `expect(b, `step ${i}, seed ${seed}`).toEqual(a)` fail -- memory aur Redis ka decision sirf `resetMs` mein 1 ms alag. Baaki sab (allowed, remaining) same.

Investigation, step by step. Pehla, reproduce: PRNG seeded hai (mulberry32), toh `seed 1` se exact same sequence dobara chalta hai -- flaky nahi, deterministic. Yahi seeded design ka fayda hai. Doosra, narrow down: step 91 tak dono agree karte the, toh logic broadly sahi hai; farak tiny hai (1 ms) aur `resetMs` mein hai jo `math.ceil(...)` se banta hai. `ceil` ka matlab ek bahut chhota float farak bhi integer boundary cross karke poora 1 ms ban sakta hai. Teesra, Redis mein state dekho: `HGETALL` us key ka -- tokens string 14 significant digits ka. TypeScript ka state print karo. Ab Lua padho: `tokens` variable full precision hai, `tostring` sirf HSET mein lagta hai, aur `reset` usi full variable se banta hai.

Cause: pehle TypeScript version ne tokens ko pehle `luaToString` se round kiya aur phir REPLY bhi rounded value se banaya. Redis reply full precision se banata hai. Jab `(capacity - tokens) * 1000 / rate` exactly ek integer ke paas tha, rounded value ek taraf gayi aur full value doosri taraf -- 1135 vs 1136.

Fix: reply full-precision `tokens` se, store rounded `luaToString(tokens)`. Code comment ab yahi bolta hai. Aur mutation L1 confirm karta hai ki rounding bhi zaroori hai: stored value round na karo toh parity fail.

Lesson: aise bugs normal unit tests kabhi nahi pakadte -- 91 random steps ke baad ek specific float combination chahiye tha. Isliye random, seeded, real-Redis parity test.

real_world_analogy: Do ghadiyan 91 minute tak same time dikhati hain, phir ek second ka farak. Pata chala ek ghadi second ko round karke dikhati hai aur andar bhi rounded time hi chalati hai; doosri andar exact chalti hai aur sirf screen par round karti hai.
how_it_works: Parity loop: har step `t += floor(rand * maxAdvanceMs)`, key `k0..k2`, cost 1-3; same call memory limiter aur redis limiter dono par, `toEqual` compare. Failure message mein step aur seed -- replay possible.

Token bucket parity: `tokenBucket({ capacity: 5, refillPerSec: 3 })`, seeds 1, 2, 3, 200 steps each, max advance 700 ms. Fix `src/algorithms.ts` `tokenBucket` step mein. question: In the first mutation run, mutations L3 and M3 survived. What does a surviving mutant tell you, and how was each of these two handled differently?
answer_hinglish:
Mutation testing mein code mein jaan-boojh ke ek bug daalte hain aur poora suite chalate hain. Koi test fail hua -> mutant 'caught'. Koi fail nahi hua -> 'survived'. Survivor ka matlab teen mein se ek hai: test gap (code ka behaviour tested nahi), redundant code (jo code badla woh kuch karta hi nahi), ya equivalent mutant (by design koi farak padta hi nahi). Debugging ka kaam yeh decide karna hai ki kaunsa case hai.

L3: 'a clock going backwards changes tokens' -- yani token bucket mein `Math.max(now - ts, 0)` ka guard hata do, toh clock peeche jaane par negative elapsed tokens GHATA deta hai. Pehle run mein yeh survive hua. Matlab clock-backwards ka test yeh prove nahi kar raha tha ki tokens remove nahi hote. Yeh test gap tha, toh test sharp kiya: ab test 'a clock going backwards neither adds nor REMOVES tokens' -- capacity 10, ek consume (9 left), clock -5000 ms, agla consume `remaining: 8` expect karta hai; comment kehta hai bina guard ke 3 bachte. Final run mein L3 = 1 failed test. Distributed angle: injected app clocks drift karein toh yeh guard hi bachata hai.

M3: 'the memory store ignored its expiry'. Survive hua kyunki expiry kabhi decision badalti hi nahi thi: idle bucket waise bhi full refill ho jaata hai, aur do window purani state kabhi match nahi hoti. Yeh redundant code tha, test gap nahi. Toh test nahi, CODE badla: expiry hata di. Uski jagah ek test likha jo yeh property prove karta hai -- 'a long-idle key behaves exactly like a new one': ek din baad key ka decision fresh key ke barabar. Memory ab `maxKeys` (LRU) se bounded hai.

To ek survivor ne test sudhaara, doosre ne code ghataya.
why_needed: Coverage percentage batata hai code chala ya nahi; mutation testing batata hai ki tests sach mein galat behaviour pakadte hain ya nahi. Survivors ka sahi interpretation senior skill hai.
real_world_analogy: Fire drill mein ek alarm jaan-boojh ke band karo. Kisi ko pata nahi chala? Ya toh drill ka checklist kamzor hai (L3), ya woh alarm us kamre mein tha jahan koi jaata hi nahi -- alarm hi hatao (M3).

question: Two mutants, S6 and H5, survived the final run and are documented as equivalent. How do you prove a mutant is equivalent rather than a missing test?
answer_hinglish:
Equivalent ka matlab hai: mutated code har possible input par original jaisa hi behave karta hai, toh koi bhi test use pakad nahi sakta. Proof ek argument hai -- 'yeh values kabhi aisi ho hi nahi sakti jahan farak pade' -- sirf 'mujhe test nahi soojha' nahi.

S6: 'retry may be 0 when denied' -- sliding window mein `Math.max(retry, 1)` hata do. Kya retry kabhi 0 ho sakta hai? Retry do candidates ka minimum hai. Pehla `window - elapsed`: `elapsed = now - curStart` aur `curStart = now - (now % window)`, toh `elapsed = now % window`, jo hamesha `< window` -- toh yeh >= 1 ms (integer ms). Doosra `Math.ceil((needed / prev) * window)` sirf tab jab `prev > 0`; denial ka matlab `estimated + cost > limit`, toh `needed > 0`, toh ceil >= 1. Dono >= 1, toh `max(.., 1)` kabhi value nahi badalta. Kept kyun? Lua script mein `math.max(retry, 1)` hai aur TS usko mirror karta hai -- parity ke liye code shape same rakha. Code comment bhi yahi kehta hai.

H5: 'IPv6 zone id not stripped'. Zone id (`%eth0`) address ke END par hota hai -- last group mein. IPv6 key /64 hai, yani pehle 4 groups. Toh zone strip ho ya na ho, key same -- README ka argument yahi hai. Clarity ke liye kept.

Jo bhi equivalent claim karo, README mein reason likho -- taaki agle run mein koi 'naya test gap' na samjhe. Aur U1-U3 Lua mutations real Redis tests se pakdi gayi, equivalent nahi.

how_it_works: Equivalence proof = input domain ka invariant dikhana: S6 mein `0 <= elapsed < window` aur denial par `needed > 0`; H5 mein zone id sirf address ke end mein aur key sirf first 4 hextets.

question: After deploying three instances, support reports that some users get about three times their limit. How do you investigate?
answer_hinglish:
Sabse pehle shak: limit shared nahi hai -- har instance apna alag count rakh raha hai. '3 instances, 3x limit' exactly MemoryStore ka signature hai. README warn karta hai: 'N instances each with their own MemoryStore allow up to N x the limit', aur load test mein yahi measure hua: limit 500, memory mode mein 1116 allowed.

Investigation order:

1. Config check: limiter ka `store` kya hai? `new MemoryStore()` (jaise README ka `apiLimit` example, jo 'single instance / dev' ke liye hai) ya `new RedisStore(...)`? Ek environment variable galat ho toh production mein bhi memory chal sakti hai.

2. Degraded mode: FailoverStore lagaya hai toh shayad Redis down ya slow tha aur fallback chal raha tha. Decisions par `degraded: true` aata hai, aur `onError` callback mein errors log hone chahiye (README example `logger.warn(..., "rate-limit store failed")`). Logs mein yeh warning dikhe toh cause Redis connectivity hai, limiter nahi.

3. Redis mein keys dekho: `redis-cli --scan --pattern 'rl:*'` -- user ki key hai? Uski value (token bucket ka `HGETALL`, sliding window ke counter keys) request count se match karti hai?

4. Prefix aur key: teeno instances same `prefix` aur same key function use karte hain? Agar ek instance ka key IP par hai aur trusted proxy setting alag hai (`trustedProxies`), toh same user ki alag keys ban sakti hain.

5. Tests: CI mein Redis tests sach mein chale ya SKIP hue? Bina Redis ke `[redis.test] SKIPPED` notice print hota hai -- green run ka matlab yeh nahi ki multi-instance test chala.

Fix usually: production mein RedisStore, aur Redis outage ke liye degraded metric par alert.
why_needed: Yeh real production complaint ka shape hai. Systematic checklist se root cause minutes mein milta hai, guesswork se ghanton mein.
real_world_analogy: Teen gates par teen guards, har ek apni diary mein ginta hai. Ek visitor teeno gates se ghoom ke teen guna andar aata hai. Pehla sawaal: kya guards ek shared register use kar rahe hain?
how_it_works: MemoryStore per-process Map hai. RedisStore ek shared key par atomic script. FailoverStore primary fail hone par fallback use karta hai aur `degraded: true` lagata hai. Prefix + key milkar Redis key banate hain.
in_this_project: `src/memory-store.ts` comment 'N instances -> up to N x the limit'; `src/failover-store.ts` (`onError`, `degraded`); `src/limiter.ts` (prefix + key); `test/redis.test.ts` aur `test/express.test.ts` ka skip notice; load test result `bench/reference-results/2026-11-23-win32-load-run1.json`: memory-shared `allowed: 1116` vs redis-shared `allowed: 500`.

question: Write a hash-tag key helper so the sliding window's derived keys land in the same Redis Cluster slot, plus a test that proves it. (Not in the repo.)
answer_hinglish:
Yeh is repo mein NAHI hai -- README Redis Cluster ko 'NOT tested' aur hash tag ko 'not done or tested here' bolta hai. Exercise yeh hai ki minimal, safe helper banao aur slot-level test likho, bina Lua script badle.

Idea: Cluster slot = CRC16 of key mod 16384, par agar key mein `{...}` hai (non-empty) toh sirf braces ke andar ka part hash hota hai. Sliding window script `KEYS[1]` (base key) se `KEYS[1] .. ':' .. cur_start` banata hai. Agar base key `rl:login:{email:a@b.com}` hai, toh derived keys bhi `{email:a@b.com}` hi hash karengi -- teeno same slot.

Helper ke rules: (1) id ko braces mein lapeto; (2) id mein khud `{` ya `}` ho toh reject karo -- warna pehla `{...}` pair galat jagah ban sakta hai aur attacker apni key ka slot control kar sakta hai; (3) empty id reject (empty `{}` hash tag ignore hota hai). Prefix braces ke BAHAR rehna chahiye -- `{rl}` jaisa constant tag sab clients ko ek slot (ek node) par daal deta.

Test: `cluster-key-slot` package (ioredis ki dependency, `node_modules` mein maujood) ka default export use karo -- ek function jo key ka slot deta hai (test mein naam `calculateSlot` rakha hai). Base key aur kuch window starts ke derived keys ka slot same hona chahiye; aur do alag users ke keys ka slot (generally) alag hona chahiye taaki load spread ho. Yeh test single-node par bhi chal sakta hai kyunki yeh sirf slot calculation hai -- real cluster test alag se chahiye (docker cluster) jo is exercise ke bahar hai.

Use: `limiter.consume(clusterKey(`email:${email}`))` -- RateLimiter prefix lagayega: `rl:login:{email:...}`. Key length 512 limit ke andar rakhna padega.
why_needed: Cluster par multi-key Lua ka standard fix hash tags hain; ise khud likh ke test karna dikhata hai ki tum slot mechanics samajhte ho, sirf naam nahi jaante.
real_world_analogy: Ek courier company pincode se warehouse chunti hai. Teen parcel ek saath deliver karne hain toh teeno par same pincode ka sticker lagao -- baaki address kuch bhi ho, warehouse ek hi hoga.
how_it_works: Slot function: braces ka pehla `{` aur uske baad ka pehla `}` dhundta hai; beech mein kuch ho toh sirf woh hash hota hai. Isliye id ke andar braces allow karna dangerous hai.
in_this_project: Abhi `src/limiter.ts` key ko as-is prefix ke saath use karta hai (`this.prefix + key`) aur `src/lua/sliding_counter.lua` `KEYS[1] .. ':' .. cur_start` se keys banata hai. Helper `src/adapters/http.ts` ke `ipKey` ki tarah ek chhota pure function ho sakta hai. `cluster-key-slot` `projects/19-rate-limit/node_modules` mein ioredis ke through installed hai, par package.json ki direct dependency nahi.

Pure function -- aasaan test
Slot spread bhi test hota hai
disadvantages: Sirf slot math test hota hai, real cluster behaviour nahi
User ko helper use karna yaad rakhna padega
common_mistakes: Poore prefix ko braces mein daalna (`{rl:login}`) -- sab ek slot par
Id ke andar ke braces allow karna
Sirf token bucket test karke sliding window bhool jaana
follow_up_questions: RateLimiter mein hi option `cluster: true` daalna better hoga?
50 users mein se 40+ alag slots ka assertion flaky ho sakta hai kya?
Real Redis Cluster test kaise setup karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Helper (opt-in, simple) vs RateLimiter mein built-in cluster mode (automatic, par API complex) vs script badal ke keys declare karna (contract-correct, app clock chahiye). Helper sabse kam invasive hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Hash tag bhoolna -> cross-slot error -> store error path. Constant tag -> hot node. Id mein braces -> attacker slot choose kar sakta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Sliding window state ek hash key mein (fields = window starts) -- ek key, koi tag nahi chahiye, par Lua script badalna padega; ya app-computed KEYS.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Per-client tag ka matlab load clients ke saath spread hota hai -- 100x users par bhi theek. Ek hi bahut hot client (shared key, jaise load test ka 'shared') ek slot par rahega -- us case mein sharding help nahi karti.

question: Write a node-redis adapter for RedisStore and a test that runs it against a real Redis. (The README documents the adapter but says it is not tested; it is not in the repo.)
answer_hinglish:
README aur `redis-store.ts` ka comment node-redis ke liye adapter ka shape dete hain, par yeh 'documented, not tested' hai aur `node-redis` package is repo mein install bhi nahi hai. Exercise: adapter ko ek function banao aur ek real-Redis test likho jo `ioredisClient` wale tests ka mirror ho.

Adapter: `RedisScriptClient` ke do methods. node-redis v4 mein `client.evalSha(sha, { keys, arguments })` aur `client.scriptLoad(script)` hain. Toh `evalsha: (sha, keys, args) => client.evalSha(sha, { keys, arguments: args })`. Structural type rakho (node-redis import mat karo) taaki package ki zero runtime dependency bachi rahe -- `ioredisClient` ka bhi yahi pattern hai.

Sabse important test NOSCRIPT ka hai. `RedisStore` NOSCRIPT ko `String(error.message).includes("NOSCRIPT")` se pehchanta hai. Agar node-redis ka error message alag format mein ho (jaise error object ka shape alag), toh retry kabhi nahi hoga aur Redis restart ke baad har request fail. Isliye test: ek consume, `SCRIPT FLUSH`, phir consume -- `{ allowed: true, remaining: 1 }` aana chahiye.

Doosra test: reply shape. node-redis integer replies ko JS numbers deta hai; `toDecision` `typeof x === "number"` check karta hai. Agar kabhi RESP3 ya koi option strings/BigInt de, toh 'unexpected reply' error aayega -- test pakdega.

Teesra: atomicity ek chhote version mein (2 clients, 100 requests, capacity 20 -> exactly 20).

Redis na ho toh `describe.skipIf` se skip with notice -- repo ka existing convention.
why_needed: Bring-your-own-client design tabhi kaam ka hai jab har adapter ke saath woh edge cases (NOSCRIPT, reply types) verify hon jo store assume karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek universal charger ka naya plug adapter: sirf 'fit ho gaya' kaafi nahi, check karo current sahi direction mein aata hai (NOSCRIPT detection) aur voltage sahi hai (reply types).
how_it_works: Adapter sirf method signatures map karta hai. `RedisStore` ke assumptions: error message mein 'NOSCRIPT' text, `scriptLoad` SHA string return kare, reply array of numbers ho.

question: The tests show 'exactly 50 of 300' and 'exactly 500' under load. What consistency guarantee does this rate limiter really give, and under which conditions does it break?
answer_hinglish:
Guarantee: ek single Redis primary ke andar, ek key ke liye, decisions linearizable hain -- har request ka script ek total order mein chalta hai aur har script pichle ka likha state dekhta hai. Isliye 'at most limit' bhi aur 'exactly limit' bhi, chahe kitne app instances hon. Evidence: 3 clients x 300 -> 50; 2 clients x 200 sliding -> 40; do Express instances, 30 requests -> 10; load test run 1, 3 processes -> 500 of 500.

Kab tootta hai -- aur yeh list hi senior answer hai:

1. Store Redis nahi hai: MemoryStore ya FailoverStore ka fallback -> per instance, N x limit. Decisions par `degraded: true`.
2. Redis failover: async replication se last writes lost -> over-allow.
3. Recovery: fallback counts merge nahi hote.
4. Timeout ke baad bhi execute hui call: same request do baar count -> under-allow.
5. App clocks inject kiye (`now` option): drift se token bucket free refill de sakta hai; default Redis TIME isse bachata hai.
6. Sliding window khud approximate hai: estimate assume karta hai ki pichli window ki requests evenly spread thi. Toh 'exactly 40' 'estimate ke hisaab se exactly' hai -- ek true sliding log se alag ho sakta hai. Window ke andar concurrency ka exactness alag cheez hai, algorithm ki accuracy alag.
7. Redis Cluster: tested nahi; sliding window ki undeclared keys.
8. Key design: galat `trustedProxies` ya bina IPv6 /64 grouping ke attacker ko fresh keys -- consistency sahi, par 'client' ki definition galat.

Interview mein main ise aise frame karta hoon: 'atomicity solved hai; durability aur availability trade-offs explicit aur configurable hain' -- fail open/closed per limit, aur degraded flag.
why_needed: Senior interview mein 'exactly' sunte hi follow-up aata hai: kis model mein, kin assumptions par? Clear boundary batana trust banata hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek single cashier wali dukaan mein hisaab perfect hai -- jab tak cashier wahi hai. Cashier badla, bijli gayi, ya doosri branch se bhi saaman bika -- tab hisaab ki guarantee alag hai.
how_it_works: Linearizability source: Redis ka single-threaded command execution + script atomicity. Weak points: replication (async), fallback (local), clock (injectable), algorithm (approximate estimate), routing (cluster slots).
in_this_project: Tests: `test/redis.test.ts` (atomicity), `test/express.test.ts` (two instances), `bench/load.mjs` + `bench/reference-results/2026-11-23-win32-load-run1.json`. Limits documented: README 'NOT implemented' (cluster, merge-back, cancellation). `src/types.ts` `degraded`. Sliding window approximation: `src/algorithms.ts` comment 'Approximate (exact only if the previous window's requests were evenly spread)'.
advantages: Normal operation mein exact, instance-count independent
Weak points documented aur flagged (degraded)
Failure policy per limit
disadvantages: Failover/recovery mein guarantee weak
Sliding window approximate hai
Cluster untested
common_mistakes: 'Lua atomic hai' ko 'har situation mein exact' bolna
Algorithm ki approximation aur concurrency ki exactness ko mix karna
Fallback ke decisions ko shared samajhna
follow_up_questions: Kis limit ke liye tum strict guarantee chahoge aur uski keemat kya hogi?
Sliding log se exact karte toh memory kitni lagti?
Multi-region mein ek global limit kaise doge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Single Redis = simple aur exact, par ek dependency aur ek failure domain. Strong durability ya multi-region exactness ki keemat latency hai. Project ne normal path exact aur failure path explicit-best-effort rakha.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Failover lost writes, fallback N x, recovery reset, timed-out double count, clock injection drift, cluster cross-slot -- har ek ka direction (over/under allow) alag hai aur upar list kiya.
advanced.alternatives: Per-region limits with periodic sync (eventually consistent), token leasing (instance Redis se batch mein tokens le), CRDT counters, ya ek dedicated limiter service -- PLAN ne 'distributed limits without Redis (gossip)' ko out of scope rakha.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x par same model; Redis load badhta hai. 100x par ek key ki hotness aur ek Redis ka single thread limit -- tab sharding (cluster + hash tags) ya local leasing chahiye, aur dono guarantee ko weaker banate hain.
